why_lead: The Russell 2000 ETF combined the session's broadest significant move (IWM +5.49% to 178.46 USD, Russell 2000 +5.44% versus +1.91% for the S&P 500) with a newly published, simple catalyst: October CPI flat on the month with core at a two-year low (n2184, n2183), yields 39 bps lower over 20 observations and a weaker dollar (n2258). The junk-led breadth (Plug +21.90%, Upstart +16.44%, Carvana +15.96%, Peloton +15.77%, KRE +7.36%) gives the squeeze story. Attention evidence: Tom Lee's face-ripper call and breakout coverage (n2057, n0149), small-cap shopping lists (n0920, n1996). Analog from the GFC-level bond bullishness headline (n1458) plus money-market inflows (n1454); smart-money split from Lee and Burry's closed index shorts (n1928, n0989) against Powell's hawkish remarks and Russell weakness on them (n2224, n0115) and record card debt (n0991); breaks from the 20-session Russell reference, the 2Y, Plug's filing concerns (n0741) and the pending Senate funding vote (n1532).
why_smaller: SOXL: newly published Burry bet against chip stocks (n2051) set against SOXL +10.59% (+19.03% over five sessions) and Nvidia's longest winning streak in seven years (n1020): a crowd-versus-famous-bear leverage narrative; leverage decay versus SOXX +3.70% and China export risk (n1290) supply the break. Distinct from the 2023-11-14 Nvidia copycat-hunt item.

Archer Aviation: +15.00% to 5.98 USD with an analyst-may-double story (n0942), Joby's New York air-taxi demonstration and 2025 target (n0994) and Archer's India plan (n0518): a sci-fi lottery-ticket narrative; InvestorPlace's warning, charging-standard fights (n0613, n1931) and Joby's 20-session decline supply the break.

Pfizer: contrarian bottom-fishing at a three-year low, down 50% from its 2021 peak (n0871), up only 0.97% on the small-cap squeeze day; pending obesity data (n0872) and weight-loss-stock accumulation (n0990) are the hook; job cuts (n1351) and Lilly/Novo leadership (n0852, n0865) supply the break.
